title: Close the transitive/delegated agent-config trust surface
acceptance: a PR that edits ONLY a file referenced by a floored agent-config (opencode.json/.jsonc instructions:[...] paths or globs, or an instruction-bearing prompt {file:./path}, or a CLAUDE.md @import) is graded at or above the referencing config's floor, not the default floor

reference targets are resolved deterministically from committed bytes at the canonical fork point (merge-base), never the PR head and never a scanner/heuristic; a PR cannot add or remove a reference to self-grade

CLAUDE.md @import resolution follows the first-party rule (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): every relative import (bare, ./, ../) resolves relative to the directory of the CONTAINING file, not repo-root and not the working directory; recursion capped at four hops with cycle detection; code spans, fenced blocks, and backtick-literal `@x` are skipped; out-of-repo targets (home ~, filesystem-absolute, or escaping the repo root) are skipped, in-repo parent references (@../sibling) are NOT dropped

fail closed: if a floored config's reference directives cannot be parsed at the trusted ref, verify blocks (never silently passes a referenced file at a lower tier); a {file:...} outside instruction-bearing fields (e.g. a provider apiKey) does NOT floor
no over-broad flooring: only the actually-referenced paths (or a referenced directory/glob) enter the floor set, not their whole directories

enforcement consistency: both cmdVerify and cmdTier resolve references by default so `tier` reports what the gate enforces (QRM-3.2 guarantee); a referenced path requires coverage even if it matches exempt_paths

Cursor rule references are explicitly DEFERRED from v1: .cursor/**, .cursorrules, .cursorignore remain floored directly (the config files are covered); only transitive references from a .mdc rule to a non-.cursor file are out of scope, pending first-party sourcing of the Cursor reference grammar (tracked follow-up). Deferral is documented in docs/handoffs/QRM-3.4-design.md, not silently dropped

this is a QRM-4.0 Gate prerequisite: the Gate is not complete tier-floor enforcement while a floor can be bypassed by delegation. It also surfaces a NEW QRM-4.0 prerequisite: authenticated-forge tree listing (listFiles at the trusted ref) so references resolve in forge mode
